overview: Implement and validate the Correlation Crowding-Out (CCO) phenomenon in Transformers, demonstrating that strong causal correlations drive gradient descent to suppress spurious features through occupation and crowding-out phases across synthetic, vision, and NLP tasks.

modules.name: Synthetic Causal Chain Data Generator
modules.description: Generates synthetic data following the x -> y -> z causal chain generative process, including sampling the causal parent x, the sparse quadratic response y, and the Lipschitz descendant z with configurable noise and moment bounds.

modules.name: Vision Spurious Correlation Dataset Builder
modules.description: Constructs image datasets (Waterbirds, CUB, CelebA) with controllable spurious correlation strengths between foreground/background and labels, supporting foreground-foreground and foreground-background causal disentanglement setups.

modules.name: NLP Causal Feature Masking Processor
modules.description: Preprocesses text datasets (Amazon Reviews) by separating causal features (adjectives/verbs) and spurious features (nouns), implementing logic to mask or manipulate specific feature types for evaluation.

modules.name: Simplified Two-Key Attention Network
modules.description: Implements the theoretical two-key attention model with positional encodings, two distinct key/value branches for causal and spurious inputs, and a quadratic parameterization feed-forward head.

modules.name: Transformer Model Wrappers
modules.description: Wraps standard architectures (ViT/DeiT-Small, ResNet, EfficientNet, BERT) with interfaces to extract intermediate attention weights and gradients, tailored for vision and NLP spurious correlation tasks.

modules.name: CCO-Aware Training Engine
modules.description: Orchestrates the training loop for both the simplified two-key model and standard Transformers, supporting standard empirical risk minimization and extracting per-iteration metrics for dynamics analysis.

modules.name: Multi-Phase Optimizer Scheduler
modules.description: Manages the specialized gradient descent schedules required for the two-key model, handling the distinct occupation phase (updating FFN weights only) and crowding-out phase (updating attention gate only).

modules.name: Training Dynamics Monitor
modules.description: Logs and tracks the evolution of dominant coordinate weights and attention gate probabilities during training to explicitly capture and verify the 'Occupation' and 'Crowding-out' phases of the CCO mechanism.

modules.name: Attention Map Visualizer
modules.description: Extracts and visualizes spatial attention maps from Vision Transformers at various training iterations to illustrate the shift from diffuse attention to concentrated causal feature attention.

modules.name: Feature Saliency Analyzer
modules.description: Computes and visualizes gradient-based saliency scores for NLP models to quantify the relative importance of causal versus spurious tokens across different training checkpoints.

modules.name: OOD Robustness Evaluator
modules.description: Evaluates model generalization by sweeping test-time bias strengths and measuring performance on out-of-distribution splits, calculating worst-group accuracy and test loss under distributional shifts.

modules.name: CCO Boundary Condition Analyzer
modules.description: Implements ablation scripts to test the sensitivity of the CCO phenomenon by varying the correlation gap (e.g., through label flipping probabilities) to empirically determine the threshold where cause-only prediction collapses.

modules.name: Model Comparison Benchmark Suite
modules.description: Runs comparative evaluations between Transformer architectures and CNN baselines (e.g., ResNet, EfficientNet) on identical spurious correlation datasets to validate the Transformer-specific advantage in capturing causal signals.

modules.name: Experiment Configuration Manager
modules.description: Handles YAML/JSON based configuration for dataset generation parameters, model architectures, training hyperparameters, and logging directories, ensuring reproducibility across synthetic and real-data experiments.
